records.name: Texas Workforce Commission
records.description_en: The state agency for jobs, job training, unemployment benefits, and job help for people with disabilities. It works with 28 local Workforce Solutions boards and more than 170 offices.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Any Texas worker, job seeker, or employer can use TWC services.
records.how_to_apply: Call the TWC main line or go to twc.texas.gov. Find a local Workforce Solutions office at twc.texas.gov/find-locations.
records.notes: The Austin address is the headquarters. Job seekers get in-person help at local Workforce Solutions offices.

records.name: WorkInTexas.com
records.organization: Texas Workforce Commission / Texas Workforce Solutions
records.description_en: A free state job website. You can search jobs, including state government jobs, and build a resume. There is also a phone app.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Anyone looking for work in Texas. People getting unemployment benefits must register here.
records.how_to_apply: Go to WorkInTexas.com and make a free account. Then search jobs and build or upload your resume.
records.notes: Local Workforce Solutions offices can help people who need help using the site. The unemployment benefits page confirms that claimants must register.

records.name: Unemployment Benefits
records.description_en: Short-term payments that replace part of your pay if you lost your job or your hours were cut through no fault of your own.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For workers who earned enough in the past, lost a job or hours through no fault of their own, can work, and are looking for work.
documents_needed: Names, addresses, and work dates for your past employers
records.how_to_apply: Apply online through TWC Unemployment Benefit Services (UBS) or call the Unemployment Tele-Center. You must also register on WorkInTexas.com.
records.notes: Apply soon after your job ends or your hours are cut. Claimants must keep looking for work. Tele-Center hours were not stated on the source page.

records.name: Vocational Rehabilitation (VR) Program
records.description_en: Helps people with disabilities get ready for, find, or keep a job. Services include career counseling, training, help with school, and job placement.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For adults and students with disabilities who want to work. There are also services for people who are blind or losing their vision.
documents_needed: Records about your disability (if you have them)
records.how_to_apply: Fill out the online Start My VR self-referral form, or use the TWC VR office lookup to find and call a nearby VR office.
records.notes: VR office lookup: https://webp.twc.state.tx.us/services/VRLookup/ . Also covers transition services for students with disabilities and the Criss Cole Rehabilitation Center for adults who lost their vision. VR Ombudsman: vrombudsman@twc.texas.gov.

records.name: SNAP Employment and Training (SNAP E&T)
records.organization: Texas Workforce Commission with Texas Health and Human Services Commission
records.description_en: A work program for people who get SNAP food benefits. It helps you look for work or take part in training so you can keep your food benefits.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For SNAP recipients ages 16 to 59 who can work. Adults ages 18 to 64 with no children under 14 at home can get SNAP for only 3 months in 3 years unless they work or join a work program at least 80 hours a month.
documents_needed: Any letters from TWC or HHSC about SNAP E&T
records.how_to_apply: If you get SNAP, answer any letters from the Texas Workforce Commission about SNAP E&T. Contact your local Workforce Solutions office to take part.
records.notes: People who do not have to follow basic work rules include those caring for a child under 6 or a dependent who needs help, working 30+ hours a week, getting unemployment, unable to work for health reasons, in school at least half-time, or in TANF or substance use treatment. TWC coordinates E&T through local Workforce Solutions offices.

records.name: Choices (TANF Employment Program)
records.description_en: Job help for families who get or apply for TANF cash help. It offers job search help, training, and help paying for work clothes, child care, and transportation.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For parents applying for or getting TANF cash benefits, and some parents who recently stopped getting TANF.
records.how_to_apply: Contact your local Workforce Solutions office. You may be sent to Choices after you apply for TANF.
records.notes: In two-parent families, at least one parent must meet work requirements.

records.name: WIOA Adult, Dislocated Worker, and Youth Services
records.organization: Texas Workforce Commission and local Workforce Development Boards
records.description_en: Federally funded job training and job search help. It can pay for training, help you find a job, and connect you to education.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For adults, workers who lost their jobs, and young people. Each local board sets who gets training money first.
documents_needed: Proof you can work in the U.S.
Proof of income or layoff (for some services)
records.how_to_apply: Visit a local Workforce Solutions office. There are more than 170 offices across 28 local boards.
records.notes: The source page does not list age or income rules; check with the local board. Approved schools are on TWC's Eligible Training Provider list.

records.name: Employment Service (Wagner-Peyser)
records.organization: Texas Workforce Commission and local Workforce Solutions offices
records.description_en: Free job matching and job search help at Workforce Solutions offices and on WorkInTexas.com, plus help getting back to work after a layoff.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to all job seekers.
records.how_to_apply: Sign up on WorkInTexas.com or visit a local Workforce Solutions office.
records.notes: To report fraud, call (800) 252-3642.

records.name: Adult Education and Literacy (AEL)
records.description_en: Classes in reading, writing, math, and English. Helps adults earn a GED or high school equivalency and get ready for jobs or college.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people 16 or older who are not in school (and not required to be), and who need basic skills, have no high school diploma or GED, or need to learn English.
records.how_to_apply: Call the provider hotline at (800) 441-7323 or search the Literacy Providers Directory to find a class near you.
records.cost: Not stated on source; ask the local provider
records.notes: Also offers Integrated Education and Training (IET), digital literacy, workplace literacy, family literacy, and help for internationally trained professionals. AEL program office: (737) 270-7346, AdultEducation@twc.texas.gov.

records.name: Skills Development Fund
records.description_en: State grants that pay for custom job training for workers at Texas businesses. Colleges and partners teach the training.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For businesses working with a community or technical college, TEEX, or a workforce board. Trainees must be full-time W-2 employees.
records.how_to_apply: Employers contact a TWC regional business liaison. TWC takes proposals all year.
records.notes: Employer-driven; individuals cannot apply directly. Businesses can get up to $500,000; average cost per trainee is $2,400; grants usually last 12 months.

records.name: Skills for Small Business
records.description_en: Pays for training at community or technical colleges for new and current workers at small businesses.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For businesses with fewer than 100 employees. Training is for full-time employees.
records.how_to_apply: Employers apply online through the Skills for Small Business application on the TWC page.
records.notes: Employer-driven. Up to $2,000 per new employee and $1,000 per current employee.

records.name: Self-Sufficiency Fund
records.description_en: Training grants that help people on public help or with low incomes earn job credentials through colleges and nonprofits.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For adults on SNAP or TANF, people at risk of needing public help, workers earning under $37,000 a year with a dependent child, and low-income youth ages 18 to 24.
records.how_to_apply: Trainees sign up through a community or technical college or nonprofit that has a Self-Sufficiency Fund grant. Organizations apply to TWC.
records.notes: Grants go to colleges and 501(c)(3) nonprofits, not directly to individuals.

records.name: Registered Apprenticeship Programs
records.description_en: Earn money while you learn a skilled trade. Apprenticeships mix paid on-the-job training with classes.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For job seekers who want to learn a trade. Each program sets its own entry rules.
records.how_to_apply: Visit a local Workforce Solutions office or TWC's find-apprenticeships page to learn about openings.
records.notes: Email: apprenticeshiptexas@twc.texas.gov.

records.name: Veteran Employment Services
records.description_en: Veterans get priority job help, training, and career support at Workforce Solutions offices. Programs include the Texas Veterans Leadership Program and College Credit for Heroes.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For veterans and military service members.
documents_needed: DD-214 or other proof of service
records.how_to_apply: Visit a local Workforce Solutions office and tell staff you are a veteran, or contact the Texas Veterans Leadership Program.
records.notes: Texas Veterans Leadership Program: (512) 466-7867, tvlp@twc.texas.gov. A Homeless Veterans' Reintegration Program is also listed on the page.

records.name: Foster Youth Transition Centers and Foster Youth Services
records.description_en: Help with jobs, school, and housing resources for young people in or leaving foster care, or youth who are homeless.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Transition Centers serve youth ages 16 to 25 who are or were in foster care, are homeless, or are otherwise at risk.
records.how_to_apply: Contact TWC or your local Workforce Solutions office to find the nearest Foster Youth Transition Center.
records.notes: Related benefits include the Education and Training Voucher program and the State College Tuition Waiver (with DFPS).

records.name: Senior Community Service Employment Program (SCSEP)
records.organization: Texas Workforce Commission and SCSEP grantees
records.description_en: Paid part-time job training at nonprofits or government agencies for older adults, plus help finding a regular job.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For unemployed people age 55 or older with income at or below 125% of the federal poverty level (the source lists $13,590 a year for one person).
records.how_to_apply: Contact the SCSEP provider for your county using the provider contact list on the TWC SCSEP page.
records.notes: Texas providers: AARP Foundation, The Center for Workforce Inclusion, National Asian Pacific Center on Aging, SER-Jobs for Progress National, and Institute for Indian Development. Priority for people 65+, veterans, people with disabilities, limited English speakers, rural residents, homeless people, and people recently released from incarceration.

records.name: AARP Foundation SCSEP
records.description_en: Paid on-the-job training, about 20 hours a week at local nonprofits and public agencies, plus job placement help for older adults.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people age 55 or older who are unemployed and have low income.
records.how_to_apply: Call AARP Foundation SCSEP to see if you qualify and to find your local office.
records.notes: TWC says AARP Foundation runs SCSEP in 82 Texas counties; the county list is in TWC's SCSEP provider contact file (not captured here).

records.name: Job Corps
records.description_en: Free job training and education for young adults. Students can get free housing, meals, basic medical care, and a living allowance.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For low-income young adults ages 16 through 24 who meet income, citizenship, residency, and background rules.
records.how_to_apply: Apply online at enroll.jobcorps.gov or call 1-800-733-JOBS.
records.notes: TTY: (877) 889-5627. Texas campus locations were not confirmed this session. The site showed no enrollment pause when checked; confirm status before referring, since federal funding for Job Corps has been in flux.

records.name: Wage Claims (Texas Payday Law)
records.organization: Texas Workforce Commission, Wage and Hour Department
records.description_en: If your employer did not pay you correctly, you can file a free wage claim with TWC to try to get your pay.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For workers in Texas who were not paid wages they earned.
documents_needed: Pay stubs or records of hours worked
records.how_to_apply: File a wage claim online through the TWC Wage Claim System or call the Wage and Hour Department.
records.notes: The Texas Payday Law has a filing deadline that was not stated on the overview page; tell clients to file quickly.

records.name: Employment Discrimination Complaints
records.organization: Texas Workforce Commission, Civil Rights Division
records.description_en: Looks into complaints of job discrimination under Texas and federal law.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For workers or job applicants in Texas who think they faced discrimination at work or in hiring.
documents_needed: Notes, dates, and any records about what happened
records.how_to_apply: Use the Civil Rights Division complaint form on the TWC website or call TWC.
records.notes: Works with the U.S. EEOC. Filing deadlines apply but were not stated on the overview page.

records.name: Child Care Services (Child Care Scholarships)
records.organization: Texas Workforce Commission and local Workforce Solutions boards
records.description_en: Helps low-income families pay for child care so parents can work, look for work, or go to school.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For low-income Texas families with children who need care while parents work or go to school. Full rules are on the Texas Child Care Connection website.
records.how_to_apply: Apply online through Parent Central on childcare.texas.gov, or contact your local Workforce Solutions child care office.
records.cost: Not stated on source (families may pay a share)
records.notes: Office locator: https://www.childcare.texas.gov/office-locator . Email: ccel@twc.texas.gov. The income limit was not confirmed this session.

records.name: Workforce Solutions Alamo
records.description_en: Free job search help, career advice, and job training money through local Workforce Solutions career centers. The board also runs child care scholarships for working parents in its area.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Serves job seekers and employers in Atascosa, Bandera, Bexar, Comal, Frio, Gillespie, Guadalupe, Karnes, Kendall, Kerr, McMullen, Medina and Wilson counties. Training money and support services have extra rules, such as income limits.
documents_needed: Proof of income (for training or support programs)
records.how_to_apply: Go to the board website to find the nearest Workforce Solutions career center, or call the board office. Sign up on WorkInTexas.com to search jobs.
records.notes: Counties, address, and phone are from the TWC Workforce Development Board Directory dated July 16, 2026. The phone and address are for the board's main office, which may not be a walk-in career center. Use the website to find career center locations and hours. The website is listed on twc.texas.gov/partners/workforce-development-boards.

records.eligibility_summary_en: Serves job seekers and employers in Archer, Baylor, Clay, Cottle, Foard, Hardeman, Jack, Montague, Wichita, Wilbarger and Young counties. Training money and support services have extra rules, such as income limits.
documents_needed: Proof of income (for training or support programs)
records.how_to_apply: Go to the board website to find the nearest Workforce Solutions career center, or call the board office. Sign up on WorkInTexas.com to search jobs.
records.notes: Counties, address, and phone are from the TWC Workforce Development Board Directory dated July 16, 2026. The phone and address are for the board's main office, which may not be a walk-in career center. Use the website to find career center locations and hours. The website is listed on twc.texas.gov/partners/workforce-development-boards.
